item.title: 2026-10-05 Climate Policy & Nonprofit Governance: Clocks in parts of Canada to stay in daylight saving, but analysis backs permanent standard time
item.description: Two smaller items before you go. Parts of Canada are about to fall back into daylight saving time again this fall, even though the research keeps backing permanent standard time as the healthier option. item.title: 2026-10-05 AI & Technology: Google froze its open source bug bounty program due to a 'significant rise' in AI submissions
item.description: - Google froze a major bug bounty program because AI generated junk reports buried real security work.

item.title: 2026-10-05 Health & Fitness: Screens, Maternal Data, and Dancer Recovery Moves
item.description: - Lancet data suggests compulsive screen use, not raw hours, drives most of the harm in kids. - A CMAJ study now has hard numbers on Black maternal health gaps in Canada over a full decade. - Ottawa is consulting on why young men's mental health is sliding, worth watching for policy follow through. - Gyrotonic is moving from dance studios into trail recovery routines, a solid complement to strength work. - For a genuine digital detox weekend, there are bookable ghost towns south of the border.

item.title: 2026-10-05 Parenting: Canada Child Benefit Amounts (July 2026 to June 2027)
item.description: - Canada Child Benefit climbs in July to 8,157 dollars a year per child under six.

item.title: 2026-10-05 Sports: Jets Win, Hellebuyck Stalemate, Bombers Fall From Playoff Spot
item.description: - Jets got their first win, Kyle Connor with two power play goals in Detroit. - Hellebuyck's still suspended, no trade yet, Jets reportedly want a first-rounder and a top-six forward. - Bombers got blown out 37-10, Montreal clinched the East, Winnipeg's playoff spot is now in real danger. - Kraken crushed the Flames 6-1 in Seattle's home opener, Calgary still hasn't won. - Raptors played their first-ever game in Quebec City, lost big to Miami, 129-105.
